title: Cargo Door Latch Bracket — Temporary Impact Damage Repair

issue.reason: Original issue of the temporary reinforcing strap repair for an impact-damaged latch bracket.

abstract: Temporary repair for impact damage to a cargo door latch bracket, allowing a limited number of flight cycles while the replacement bracket is obtained, with a mandatory latch rigging check.

sections.purpose: This temporary repair allows continued operation with an impact-damaged cargo door latch bracket for a limited period while the replacement bracket is obtained.
sections.damage_assessment: Impact damage at this position almost always comes from a loading vehicle and is usually accompanied by damage to the latch access panel that is easier to see. Examine the bracket, the panel and the surrounding structure before deciding whether this repair applies. Measure the deflection of the bracket from its nominal plane with the straight edge and the feeler gauge, at the three positions marked on the repair drawing. A deflection greater than 2.5 mm at any position, any crack in the bracket, and any damage that has moved the latch shaft bore out of tolerance, all put the damage outside this repair. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the bracket radius before the repair is applied, because a crack there is not visible under the protective treatment.
sections.repair_procedure: Put the cargo door in the maintenance position, fit the door support strut and isolate the door control system. Remove the latch access panel. Clean the damaged area and remove the protective treatment locally. Blend out any raised material at the impact point with a fine abrasive, keeping within the depth limit on repair drawing RD-52-30-13-903. Install the reinforcing strap from the drawing across the deflected region, fastened to the bracket MON782098-57 with bolts LN407470-05 and to the latch stiffener D5230135108629 with bolts AGS773887-1B, at the torque values given. Do not attempt to straighten the bracket; the strap carries the load past the deflection and straightening introduces a residual stress the repair does not allow for. Apply the chemical conversion coating and the primer to the blended area. Install the latch access panel. Do the latch rigging check and confirm that the latch actuator reaches both end positions, then do the cargo door operational test and the door warning system test. The aircraft must not be released if either test fails.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is limited to 600 flight cycles or 90 days from embodiment, whichever occurs first, after which the bracket must be replaced. Do a detailed visual inspection of the strap and of the blended area, and a latch rigging check, at every 150 flight cycles. Any increase in the measured deflection makes the repair invalid immediately. The repair must be entered in the deferred defect record with its expiry and reported to Aeralis at embodiment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Bracket deflection up to 2.5 mm from nominal at any of the three measurement positions, with no crack and with the latch shaft bore inside tolerance. One bracket per door.

repair_drawings.title: Reinforcing strap, cargo door latch bracket

type_data.fastener_pattern: Eight bolts into the bracket and six into the latch stiffener, single row each side of the deflected region
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Temporary repair limited to 600 flight cycles or 90 days, whichever occurs first; inspection every 150 flight cycles.

title: Cargo Door Latch Bracket — Temporary Impact Damage Repair

issue.reason: Repair restricted to aircraft at the greased bush standard, with the rigging stack reason stated and the permanent bracket route named.

abstract: Temporary repair for impact damage to a cargo door latch bracket on aircraft at the greased bush standard, allowing a limited number of flight cycles while the replacement bracket is obtained, with a mandatory latch rigging check.

sections.purpose: This temporary repair allows continued operation with an impact-damaged cargo door latch bracket for a limited period while the replacement bracket is obtained.
sections.damage_assessment: Impact damage at this position almost always comes from a loading vehicle and is usually accompanied by damage to the latch access panel that is easier to see. Examine the bracket, the panel and the surrounding structure before deciding whether this repair applies. Establish first which latch bearing bush standard the door carries: the strap adds 1.6 mm to the stack at the bracket foot, and that thickness was allowed for against the running clearance of the greased bronze bush. On a door at the self-lubricating liner standard the shaft end float is 0.3 mm smaller and the stack closes below the rigging tolerance on the cold day case, so this repair may not be applied. Measure the deflection of the bracket from its nominal plane with the straight edge and the feeler gauge, at the three positions marked on the repair drawing. A deflection greater than 2.5 mm at any position, any crack in the bracket, and any damage that has moved the latch shaft bore out of tolerance, all put the damage outside this repair. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the bracket radius before the repair is applied, because a crack there is not visible under the protective treatment.
sections.repair_procedure: Put the cargo door in the maintenance position, fit the door support strut and isolate the door control system. Remove the latch access panel. Clean the damaged area and remove the protective treatment locally. Blend out any raised material at the impact point with a fine abrasive, keeping within the depth limit on repair drawing RD-52-30-13-903. Install the reinforcing strap from the drawing across the deflected region, fastened to the bracket MON782098-57 with bolts LN407470-05 and to the latch stiffener D5230135108629 with bolts AGS773887-1B, at the torque values given. Do not attempt to straighten the bracket; the strap carries the load past the deflection and straightening introduces a residual stress the repair does not allow for. Apply the chemical conversion coating and the primer to the blended area. Install the latch access panel. Do the latch rigging check and confirm that the latch actuator reaches both end positions, then do the cargo door operational test and the door warning system test. The aircraft must not be released if either test fails.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is limited to 600 flight cycles or 90 days from embodiment, whichever occurs first, after which the bracket must be replaced. Do a detailed visual inspection of the strap and of the blended area, and a latch rigging check, at every 150 flight cycles. Any increase in the measured deflection makes the repair invalid immediately. A door carrying this repair is excluded from the effectivity of Service Bulletin CRN-52-1015 until the bracket has been replaced; an operator who needs both takes the permanent bracket scheme offered with that campaign instead of embodying this repair first. The repair must be entered in the deferred defect record with its expiry and reported to Aeralis at embodiment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Bracket deflection up to 2.5 mm from nominal at any of the three measurement positions, with no crack and with the latch shaft bore inside tolerance. One bracket per door. Applicable only to doors at the greased bronze bush standard; not applicable to doors with self-lubricating liner bushes.
